parsed.explanation: Tier-1 exposures dominate. The state's March 2025 statute imposes birth-sex facility rules across rest stops, locker rooms, shelters, dormitories and prisons — universal, inescapable for an outed visitor — with no statewide discrimination law and a religious-refusal statute granting qualified immunity to service denials, so no working remedy exists. The parent frame adds border exposure (visa officers told to refuse on sex-discrepancy doubts; trans travellers reportedly stranded) and state-linked custody harm: federal conversion-style inmate policies and documented abuse of trans immigration detainees. The 'Worst' risk tier reflects statutes on the books, not measured incidents. Mitigating: no trans-specific criminal offence, functioning courts blocking several measures, national employment and hate-crime protection, and no documented violence pattern against visitors. Partial recourse keeps it above the 0.25 anchors; unremedied universal exclusion plus custody state hostility keeps it well below 0.45.
